summary: Same Enchantments in an item components crashes the game
description: when you have 2 enchantments "sharpness" and "minecraft:sharpness" in the new components this will crash the game 1./give @s diamond_sword[enchantments={levels:{sharpness:10,"sharpness":10}}] 2./give @s diamond_sword[enchantments={levels:{sharpness:10,"minecraft:sharpness":10}}] the second one will crash the game, but the first one doesnt.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Use the command `/give @s diamond_sword[enchantments={levels:{sharpness:10,"sharpness":10}}]`.
4. Observe that the game does not crash.
5. Use the command `/give @s diamond_sword[enchantments={levels:{sharpness:10,"minecraft:sharpness":10}}]`.
6. Observe that the game crashes.
Observed Behavior: When attempting to combine two enchantments labeled as "sharpness" and "minecraft:sharpness" on an item using the command /give @s diamond_sword[enchantments={levels:{sharpness:10,"minecraft:sharpness":10}}], the game experiences a crash. This occurs because the two enchantments are treated as identical despite their differing labels, leading to a conflict in the game's enchantment handling system. In contrast, using the command /give @s diamond_sword[enchantments={levels:{sharpness:10,"sharpness":10}}] successfully creates the item without any issues, as both enchantments are recognized as the same and do not trigger a crash. This discrepancy highlights a critical bug in the game’s enchantment processing logic, where the presence of two enchantments that are essentially the same but labeled differently causes an unexpected failure in the game's code.
Expected Behavior: When using the command to give a diamond sword with two identical enchantments, such as "sharpness" and "minecraft:sharpness," the game should successfully create the item without crashing. Instead of causing a crash, the system should recognize the duplicate enchantments and either apply the highest level or combine them appropriately, resulting in a single enchantment on the sword. This behavior should be consistent across all versions of the game.
